transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. This is an electrical safety issue. Because your washing machine is tripping the kitchen RCD (the main earth-leakage protection at your fuse box), you must stop using it until a qualified engineer has checked it. Repeatedly resetting the breaker can be dangerous if there is a live fault inside. The most common cause for this specific symptom on an Indesit washing machine is the heater element developing a leak to earth (a short circuit). This usually happens once the cycle reaches the heating stage, but it depends on exactly when the trip occurs. Other possibilities include a fault in the drain pump or damaged wiring. Please tell me: does the power go off immediately when you switch the machine on, or a few minutes later once the water has filled and started to heat up?

Thanks. It's a few minutes in, not straight away. It only seems to happen on the 40 or 60 degree washes, maybe 1 in 4 of those over the last month. Cold washes, quick 30 and rinse & spin have never tripped it. I should say I have been resetting it each time, so that's happened a fair few times now. I haven't smelled any burning or seen any sparking.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. The fact that it only trips on hot washes (40°C or 60°C) and not on cold ones points to the heater element developing a leak of electricity into the metal casing (an 'earth fault'). If that element has cracked or corroded internally, it can send current through the water and chassis, which trips your kitchen RCD. Because this is an active electrical safety hazard, please do not run any more cycles to test it further. Repeatedly resetting the trip risks causing a fire or electric shock if the insulation continues to degrade. You need to have a qualified engineer inspect the machine. They will isolate the appliance and use a multimeter to check the heater element's resistance to earth. If confirmed, they will check the heater element (and often the mounting bracket/gasket as well). If the heater tests fine, they will then check the drain pump and internal wiring for moisture or damage. Please arrange for an engineer to attend.

candidates: Heater element leaking to earth (most common) (high)
Drain pump or wiring harness shorting to earth (medium)
